bull_bear.body: Regulatory risks, market risks, operational risks
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company's focus on sustainability and renewable energy could provide a competitive advantage in the market
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend: "The Company has paid a dividend of 100% i.e., Rs. 10 per equity share of Rs. 10 each, for 2025-26 on 1 August 2026", recommended by the Board and approved by shareholders at the AGM.
- Cost of debt disclosed: average cost of long-term borrowings 7.98% and short-term borrowings 6.65% for Q1FY27.
- Inventory as the working-capital swing factor: stock as on 30 June 2026 of Rs 801 Cr (Sugar Rs 692 Cr; Molasses/Ethanol/Other Rs 109 Cr) versus Rs 923 Crores as on 30 June 2025; "Inventory carrying cost remains critical" is listed as a watch point.
- Ownership as on 30 June 2026: Promoters 60%, Individual/HUF 30%, Others 8%, FII/FPI 1%, NRI/Foreign Nationals 1%; free float 40%, market cap Rs 940 Cr, free-float market cap Rs 373 Cr, shares outstanding 20 Cr.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Closed-loop integrated model: molasses from sugar production feeds the distillery and bagasse fuels co-generation, supporting operating efficiency, stronger margins and inter-segment resilience across the sugar-ethanol-power chain.
- Deep, long-standing farmer relationships — sourced cane from ~2.54 lakh farmers in FY26 with disciplined cane payments within 12-13 days of delivery, reinforcing farmer trust and continued cane supply.
- Established distribution network of wholesalers and brokers/sub-brokers across six States, with each wholesaler relationship over five years old, indicating reliable, sticky market reach.
- Direct supply agreements with major Oil Marketing Companies for ethanol under the government-contracted Ethanol Blended Petrol programme, providing revenue stability.
- Stable, experienced workforce with 77% of employees associated with the Company for over five years, reflecting continuity and domain expertise.
- Robust credit profile — long-term rating reaffirmed at IND A+/Stable and short-term at IND A1 by India Ratings and Research, reflecting debt-repayment capability and financial governance.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sugar price volatility — Management explicitly names sugar price volatility as a structural risk it manages through R&D, farmer outreach and operational efficiency programmes.
- Sugar recovery rate fluctuations — Recovery-rate variability is flagged by management alongside sugar price volatility as a structural risk requiring proactive mitigation (agronomic practices, operational efficiency).
- Government-regulated cane cost (State Advised Price) versus market-determined sugar prices — Cane cost is set administratively via the SAP mechanism while sugar is sold at market prices, creating a structural cost-price mismatch risk that management specifically calls out.
- Dependence on government policy support across the value chain — Sector economics rely on continued government support — cane SAP fixation, transportation reimbursement, ethanol blending (EBP) mandates, and export-duty/quota decisions — any policy reversal is a structural exposure.
- Crude-oil price volatility and geopolitical disruption — India imports ~85% of its crude oil requirement; oil-price swings and Middle East geopolitical tensions/shipping disruptions cascade into inflation, logistics costs and the fiscal balance, indirectly affecting ethanol-blending economics that the Company's distillery segment depends on.
- Single-state (Uttar Pradesh) manufacturing concentration — All four of the Company's sugar mills are located in Uttar Pradesh, concentrating operational, weather and state-policy risk in a single geography.
- Margin/profitability sensitivity — FY26 operating profit margin fell 28.30% and net profit margin fell 36.23% year-on-year, with return on net worth down 36.18%, all attributed by the Company to lower profitability — underscoring earnings' sensitivity to cane-cost and sugar-price cycles.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Lineage and structure: "Avadh Sugar & Energy Ltd incorporated in 1932 (Group in Sugar Business over 9 decades), pursuant to the scheme of merger and demerger this company formed in 2015, Manufacturing Sugar, Ethanol and Power" — the deck carries both the 1932 incorporation and the 2015 formation.
- Patronage of the K.K. Birla Group, "Established in 1932 by Late Dr. Krishna Kumar Birla", with claims of "Excellent Corporate Governance" and "Highly Experienced Management".
- Strategic location in Uttar Pradesh, described as the "largest Sugar producing State in India"; four units span West, Central and East UP (Seohara, Rosa, Hargaon, Hata).
- Reach and standing: 2.9 lac farmers connected, distribution across 6 states, and a long-term credit rating of A+.
- Three-engine framing: sugar as "A Disciplined Core Business Anchors Earnings Through The Cycle", distillery as "A Non-cyclical Earnings Lever Embedded Within The Sugar Ecosystem", and co-gen as "Value Extraction Beyond Sugar With Limited Downside Risk".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Cane pricing] "The Government raises Sugarcane FRP for SS 2026-27 by 2.81% to Rs. 365/qtl. up from Rs. 355/qtl."; a listed risk is an FRP/SAP increase "without corresponding sugar price increases".
- [Ethanol policy] "Ethanol blending has reached 20% as on 30 June 2026, on course to achieve target of 20%", with blending progressing 10.02% (ESY 21-22) to 19.17% (ESY 24-25); NITI Aayog "is working on a roadmap for blending targets beyond E20". OMC contracted quantity shown at 1,132 Cr Ltrs in ESY 24-25 and 1,048 Cr Ltrs for ESY 25-26 till 30 June 2026.
- [Company ethanol allocation] For ESY 2025-26 up to 24 July 2026 the company's own allocation/supply (Cr Ltrs) was Juice 1.71 allocated / 1.69 supplied, B-Heavy 4.78 / 3.69, C-Heavy 1.05 / 0.99 — total 7.54 allocated against 6.37 supplied.
- [Supply-demand] Company estimate for SS 2025-26: opening stock 47.00 lac tons, production 278.00, total availability 325.00, domestic consumption 270.00, exports 8.00, closing stock 47.00 — "sufficient to meet around two month's domestic consumption"; exports for SS 2026-27 depend on post-monsoon production estimates "only after September 2026".
- [Regulatory intervention] "To moderate the recent increase in sugar prices, the Government has imposed stock holding limits of up to 4,000 quintals of sugar at any time or location for every dealer."
- [Competition for cane] "Competition from the jaggery and khandsari sectors is expected to intensify due to the growing demand for natural sweeteners, which may impact cane availability for sugar mills."
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Avadh Sugar & Energy Limited, part of the K.K. Birla Group, manufactures white crystal sugar and refined sugar from sugarcane at four plants in Uttar Pradesh, and converts by-products downstream into ethanol (fuel-grade and industrial), spirits, and co-generated power. Sugar is sold in bulk (mainly 50 kg packs) to wholesalers, institutional buyers and trade partners; ethanol is supplied to Oil Marketing Companies under the government's Ethanol Blended Petrol programme; surplus power is supplied to the state grid.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body: In line with its strategy to move beyond commodity dependence, a refinery is being developed at Rosa to manufacture value-added sugar products. Separately, to extend operational continuity beyond the traditional crushing cycle, a multi-feed distillery is being developed at Rosa. During 2025-26, mill house modernisation was undertaken with new installations at Seohara and Rosa. Following recent expansion, distillery operations achieved 83% capacity utilisation in 2025-26.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global sugar prices remain closely linked to crude oil and ethanol dynamics: when oil prices rise, mills divert more cane toward ethanol production, while weaker oil prices shift more cane back into sugar — a mix lever relevant to the Company's own sugar/ethanol feedstock allocation.
- Global sugar markets have stabilised after two years of volatility, with stronger harvests and improved rainfall across Asia and increased output from key producers (India, Thailand, Pakistan, Brazil) restoring balance to a market that had remained in deficit through 2023/24.
- In 2026, sugar price movements are expected to be driven more by competition among exporting countries and the timing of export releases rather than by fears of physical shortages, with simultaneous large export releases a risk to prices.
- India's net sugar production is estimated to surge ~6.50% year-on-year to 37.9 Million Tonnes, driven by favourable weather, expanded planting area and improved yields following recovery from El Nino impacts, with higher production likely to boost both exports and ending stocks.
- For the 2025-26 crushing season, India's sugar production is estimated at 27.90 Million Tonnes, a recovery from ~26.20 Million Tonnes in 2024-25 (after ethanol diversion adjustments), supported by improved cane availability and policy recalibration.
- Global sugar consumption growth remains moderate and insufficient to fully offset rising global production, contributing to a relatively balanced-to-surplus market outlook, while developed-market demand is flat-to-declining due to health trends and alternative sweeteners, with growth concentrated in emerging economies.

- Global sugar markets have stabilised after two years of volatility, with stronger harvests and improved rainfall across Asia and increased output from key producers (India, Thailand, Pakistan, Brazil) restoring balance to a market that had remained in deficit through 2023/24.
- In 2026, sugar price movements are expected to be driven more by competition among exporting countries and the timing of export releases rather than by fears of physical shortages, with simultaneous large export releases a risk to prices.
- India's net sugar production is estimated to surge ~6.50% year-on-year to 37.9 Million Tonnes, driven by favourable weather, expanded planting area and improved yields following recovery from El Nino impacts, with higher production likely to boost both exports and ending stocks.
- For the 2025-26 crushing season, India's sugar production is estimated at 27.90 Million Tonnes, a recovery from ~26.20 Million Tonnes in 2024-25 (after ethanol diversion adjustments), supported by improved cane availability and policy recalibration.
- Global sugar consumption growth remains moderate and insufficient to fully offset rising global production, contributing to a relatively balanced-to-surplus market outlook, while developed-market demand is flat-to-declining due to health trends and alternative sweeteners, with growth concentrated in emerging economies.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: In line with its strategy to move beyond commodity dependence, a refinery is being developed at Rosa to manufacture value-added sugar products. Separately, to extend operational continuity beyond the traditional crushing cycle, a multi-feed distillery is being developed at Rosa. During 2025-26, mill house modernisation was undertaken with new installations at Seohara and Rosa. Following recent expansion, distillery operations achieved 83% capacity utilisation in 2025-26.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Closed-loop integrated model: molasses from sugar production feeds the distillery and bagasse fuels co-generation, supporting operating efficiency, stronger margins and inter-segment resilience across the sugar-ethanol-power chain.
- Deep, long-standing farmer relationships — sourced cane from ~2.54 lakh farmers in FY26 with disciplined cane payments within 12-13 days of delivery, reinforcing farmer trust and continued cane supply.
- Established distribution network of wholesalers and brokers/sub-brokers across six States, with each wholesaler relationship over five years old, indicating reliable, sticky market reach.
- Direct supply agreements with major Oil Marketing Companies for ethanol under the government-contracted Ethanol Blended Petrol programme, providing revenue stability.
- Stable, experienced workforce with 77% of employees associated with the Company for over five years, reflecting continuity and domain expertise.
- Robust credit profile — long-term rating reaffirmed at IND A+/Stable and short-term at IND A1 by India Ratings and Research, reflecting debt-repayment capability and financial governance.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Cane pricing] "The Government raises Sugarcane FRP for SS 2026-27 by 2.81% to Rs. 365/qtl. up from Rs. 355/qtl."; a listed risk is an FRP/SAP increase "without corresponding sugar price increases".
- [Ethanol policy] "Ethanol blending has reached 20% as on 30 June 2026, on course to achieve target of 20%", with blending progressing 10.02% (ESY 21-22) to 19.17% (ESY 24-25); NITI Aayog "is working on a roadmap for blending targets beyond E20". OMC contracted quantity shown at 1,132 Cr Ltrs in ESY 24-25 and 1,048 Cr Ltrs for ESY 25-26 till 30 June 2026.
- [Company ethanol allocation] For ESY 2025-26 up to 24 July 2026 the company's own allocation/supply (Cr Ltrs) was Juice 1.71 allocated / 1.69 supplied, B-Heavy 4.78 / 3.69, C-Heavy 1.05 / 0.99 — total 7.54 allocated against 6.37 supplied.
- [Supply-demand] Company estimate for SS 2025-26: opening stock 47.00 lac tons, production 278.00, total availability 325.00, domestic consumption 270.00, exports 8.00, closing stock 47.00 — "sufficient to meet around two month's domestic consumption"; exports for SS 2026-27 depend on post-monsoon production estimates "only after September 2026".
- [Regulatory intervention] "To moderate the recent increase in sugar prices, the Government has imposed stock holding limits of up to 4,000 quintals of sugar at any time or location for every dealer."
- [Competition for cane] "Competition from the jaggery and khandsari sectors is expected to intensify due to the growing demand for natural sweeteners, which may impact cane availability for sugar mills."
